clue.text: Advocate of drink followed by drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A drinker who backs having one drink after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followed by' just places the second drink after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate argues for a cause, as a backer or champion of it does.

clue.text: Cry tears regularly becoming dry

parts.note: to sob is to cry

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter of the word that follows is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Someone weeping as they finally give up drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry describes a person who no longer drinks alcohol, the same as being teetotal.

clue.text: Urge head of board to provide transport for young

parts.note: to push someone is to urge them on
the chair presides over a board meeting

explanation.surface: Pressing the company chairman to lay on a school bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of board' is not the first letter B: it is the person at the head of a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled seat pushed along carrying a baby or toddler is a vehicle for small children.

clue.text: Professed nothing reasonable over time

parts.note: zero, nought

indicators.note: the sensible word is placed over, covering, the time letter so it ends up inside

parts.note: sensible means reasonable
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone claiming to have no sensible ideas left after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside SENSIBLE after its first letter, giving STENSIBLE, and O goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means apparent or claimed outwardly, as a professed reason is stated but perhaps not real.

clue.text: Touchy feline climbing on bit of roof

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing means reading upwards, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a cat is a feline
roofs are covered in tiles

explanation.surface: A prickly cat scrambling up onto the roof tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touchy' looks like irritable, but it is the definition in its literal sense of relating to touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to the sense of feel, so it is touchy in the most literal way.

clue.text: About to get freebie for retirement

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a treat is something given free as a gift

explanation.surface: A worker on the point of receiving a free gift on leaving the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests ending work, but here it is the act of withdrawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a withdrawal into seclusion, and retirement can mean withdrawing to a quiet place.

clue.text: Foundation degree by half-sibling

parts.note: a Bachelor of Arts degree
sis, short for sister, is a sibling cut down, half of the full word

explanation.surface: A foundation degree earned by a stepbrother or stepsister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-sibling' looks like a stepsister, but it means a sibling word cut in half: sis from sister.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the underlying support on which something rests, just like a foundation.

clue.text: Preclude loud vomit

parts.note: to bar is to prevent or rule out
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: Ruling out any noisy throwing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Barf is American slang for throwing up, a casual synonym for being sick.

clue.text: Fish glide across the ice

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flat sea fish related to the ray
second meaning: move over ice on blades

explanation.surface: A fish sliding along over a frozen pond.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a flat cartilaginous sea creature and also the verb for moving on blades over a rink.

clue.text: Small, quiet Liberal speaks and chokes

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
L is the abbreviation for a Liberal
to utter is to speak

explanation.surface: A timid little Liberal politician tries to talk and gags on the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who splutters makes spitting choking noises, coughing and struggling to get words out.

clue.text: Torment and ecstasy in finest surroundings

indicators.note: in places the drug letter within the word for finest
surroundings means the word for finest wraps around the other piece

parts.note: best means finest
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Agony and bliss experienced in the most luxurious setting.
explanation.definitionFit: To beset is to trouble or harass persistently, as torment does, a verb in both cases.

clue.text: Aware Cult with New Order produces discordant shriek

indicators.note: a new order of letters is exactly a rearrangement, with the band name as disguise

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Two bands share a bill and make an unholy racket together.
explanation.walkthrough: New Order is a Manchester band, so the clue reads like a gig review; here the name signals a reordering.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterwaul is a yowling cry like that of a cat on heat, harsh and jarring.

clue.text: Drew back while accepting first parts of national curriculum, as agreed

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the initials go inside the drew-back word

parts.note: to recoil is to draw back in alarm

indicators.note: the first parts of the words means taking each one's opening letter

parts.note: initial letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Teachers flinched at the national curriculum before eventually coming round to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drew back' is past tense, which matches RECOILED; the national curriculum is the set syllabus for schools in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconciled means brought into agreement or harmony, so two settled views are agreed.

clue.text: Juliet is in France to fool around

parts.note: Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet
est is French for is

explanation.surface: Juliet goes to France to have some fun.
explanation.definitionFit: To jest is to joke or be playful, the same as clowning or larking about.

clue.text: Hot and uncommonly thick heir is one hoping for a free ride

definitions.text: one hoping for a free ride

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: uncommonly suggests the letters are set out in an unusual arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sweaty, rather dim heir thumbing a lift by the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller who thumbs lifts from passing drivers is hoping to be carried without paying.

clue.text: Study cut back at pit

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read from end to start

parts.note: to axe is to cut
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Researching job cuts made at the colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to inspect or scrutinise it closely, which is how one studies it.

clue.text: Austen novel left around, then developing into something cheesy

indicators.note: the novel and the left letter go around the reworked word

parts.note: Emma is a Jane Austen novel
L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: developing means changing shape, so the letters of then are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Austen novel turned into a corny adaptation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheesy' suggests corny, but it is literal: the answer is a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmenthal is a Swiss cheese with large holes, so it is literally a cheese-related thing.

clue.text: Broth I'm blending contains something to provide protection

indicators.note: contains says the run of letters sits inside the words in front of it

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A cook stirring soup and wearing something to guard their hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A thimble is a small cap worn on the fingertip to shield it from the needle when sewing.

clue.text: Large group of actors put on air

parts.note: broad means wide or large
the cast is the company of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A big troupe of actors giving themselves airs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on air' sounds like showing off, but it means transmitted on radio or television.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast means transmitted by radio or television, so a programme sent out is on air.

clue.text: Short time to gather in an ethical way

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
to rally is to gather together

explanation.surface: Taking a brief moment to assemble decently.
explanation.definitionFit: Morally means according to principles of right and wrong, describing conduct guided by ethics.

clue.text: Unknown Member of Parliament in government is crying loudly

parts.note: y is an unknown quantity in algebra
a group of owls is called a parliament, so an owl is one of its members
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: An obscure backbench MP in office wailing in the chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of Parliament' looks like an MP, but a parliament is the collective noun for owls.
explanation.definitionFit: Yowling is making a long, loud wailing cry, as a cat or dog does in distress.

clue.text: Giant bike missing rear end works

indicators.note: missing its rear end means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a cycle is a bike
ops is short for operations, works such as musical opuses

explanation.surface: An enormous bicycle with its back end gone, plus some factory works.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclops was a one-eyed giant of Greek myth, met by Odysseus in the Odyssey.

clue.text: Pirate's weapon sliced young woman

parts.note: to slice is to cut
a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A pirate's sword slashed a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword with a single edge, traditionally carried by sailors and buccaneers.

clue.text: Eat starters of New Orleans shrimp hash

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so the opening letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the initial letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Tucking into a menu of Louisiana seafood starters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' looks like a course on the menu, but it means the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To nosh is a British slang verb for eating, especially snacking greedily.

clue.text: Father with name that causes alarm

definitions.note: read as 'something that causes alarm', a noun

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A dad with a name that frightens people.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a device that sounds a loud warning wail, raising the alert in an emergency.

clue.text: Hip with second replacement

indicators.note: replacement suggests letters put back in different places, so the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An orthopaedic patient getting a second new hip joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip' looks like the joint, and 'second replacement' like a repeat operation; but 'Hip' is the definition in its trendy sense, and 'replacement' rearranges the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Switched on is informal for alert and up to date with fashion, which is what hip means.

clue.text: Comes close, partially within earshot

indicators.note: partially says only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the last letter of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone drawing near, half able to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' looks like the indicator, but the run starts at its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To near something is to approach it, so a person who nears is getting closer.

clue.text: Black blade gets beast

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an oar has a flat blade, and rowers call the oar itself a blade

explanation.surface: A dark sword finds its mark in a wild animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a wild pig, a large tusked animal hunted as game.

clue.text: Organ damage on vicar's insides

parts.note: harm means damage
taken as written

indicators.note: the insides of a word are its middle letters, with the outer ones removed

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The church organ wrecked, with the vicar hurt internally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' looks like a church instrument or a body part; it is the mouth organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is also called a mouth organ, a small wind instrument played by blowing and sucking.

clue.text: Knock out in the manner of French marsupial

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout
à la is French for in the style of

explanation.surface: Flattening an opponent in the Gallic style.
explanation.definitionFit: A koala is an Australian tree-dwelling animal that carries its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Deliver an ultimatum about hiding part of the moon

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the concealed run reads backwards
the words are hiding part of themselves, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the run of letters across the three words

explanation.surface: Issuing a final threat about something concealed on the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunar is the adjective relating to the Moon, from the Latin luna.

clue.text: German satirist treated stomach problem

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters of the writer are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A German comic writer receiving medical treatment for his gut.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining, a digestive ailment.
